blogPosts.title: How Much Does Concrete Floor Polishing Cost in South Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about polished concrete prices in South Melbourne? We break down the costs per square metre and what affects your final quote.
body: If you're thinking about polished concrete floors for your South Melbourne home or business, the first question is usually about cost. Prices vary depending on the condition of your slab, the finish you want, and the size of the area. For a standard grind-and-seal polish, you're looking at roughly $50 to $70 per square metre. A full high-gloss polish with multiple grinding stages can run from $65 to $90 per square metre. Epoxy coatings sit in a similar range but can go higher for custom colours or non-slip additives.

Location matters too. Because Nazcrete is based in South Melbourne, we don't slug you with travel fees for jobs in the inner suburbs. For clients in Richmond, St Kilda, or Port Melbourne, the price stays the same. However, if your property is way out in the outer suburbs like Cranbourne or Pakenham, expect a small travel surcharge. Always ask about this when getting a quote — some companies hide it in the fine print.

The condition of your existing concrete slab is the biggest variable. If it's already fairly smooth and level, you'll pay less. Cracked, uneven, or stained slabs need extra grinding and patching, which adds to the labour time. We always do a site inspection before quoting because we've seen too many cases where a phone estimate ended up way off. A proper inspection costs you nothing and gives you a real number.

Another factor is the number of grinding passes. A basic grind-and-seal might only need two passes, while a premium polished finish could need four or five, plus densifier and multiple coats of sealer. Each pass adds time and wear on diamond segments, so the price goes up. For a standard 40-square-metre living area in a South Melbourne apartment, expect the job to take two to three days.

Don't forget the extras. Moving furniture, removing old glue or coatings, and repairing major cracks all add to the cost. Some clients also want a non-slip additive mixed into the sealer, which is great for wet areas like laundry rooms or garages. We itemise everything in our quote so there are no surprises. And because we're fully insured, you're covered if anything goes wrong — peace of mind that's worth every cent.

At Nazcrete, we pride ourselves on transparent pricing. We'll walk you through each line item and explain why certain steps are needed. If you're in South Melbourne or nearby, give us a call and we'll come out for a free, no-obligation quote. Our team has done hundreds of floors across Melbourne, and we'll help you choose the finish that fits your budget and lifestyle.

blogPosts.title: Polished Concrete vs Epoxy Flooring: Which Is Better for Your Melbourne Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing between polished concrete and epoxy? We compare durability, looks, cost and maintenance for Melbourne homes and garages.
body: One of the most common questions we get at Nazcrete is whether polished concrete or epoxy flooring is the better choice. Both have their strengths, but the right answer depends on where you're installing it and what you need from the floor. Polished concrete is essentially the slab itself ground down and sealed, while epoxy is a coating applied on top. Each has a different feel, durability, and price point.

Polished concrete is ideal for living areas, open-plan kitchens, and retail spaces in Melbourne. It's extremely durable, low maintenance, and gives a sleek, natural look that doesn't chip or peel. Because it's the actual concrete, there's no coating to wear off over time. It handles heavy foot traffic beautifully and can last decades with minimal care. A simple mop and occasional re-seal every few years keeps it looking great.

Epoxy flooring, on the other hand, is a thick plastic coating that bonds to the concrete. It's fantastic for garages, workshops, and warehouses because it's resistant to chemicals, oil spills, and heavy machinery. Epoxy also comes in a huge range of colours and patterns, including metallic and flake finishes. However, it can chip if something heavy is dropped on it, and once damaged, the coating needs to be repaired or replaced in that spot.

Cost-wise, both are comparable for standard installations. Polished concrete might be slightly cheaper if your slab is in good condition, while epoxy can be more expensive if you want decorative flakes or metallic pigments. In a Melbourne climate, both handle temperature changes well, but direct sunlight can cause epoxy to yellow over time if not UV-stabilised. Polished concrete doesn't have that issue.

Maintenance is where polished concrete wins for most homeowners. You don't need special cleaners — just warm water and a neutral pH cleaner. Epoxy needs to be kept clean to avoid scratches from grit, and it can show wear in high-traffic areas sooner. For a family home in South Melbourne or St Kilda, we usually recommend polished concrete for living spaces and epoxy for the garage.

At Nazcrete, we've installed both systems across hundreds of Melbourne properties. We can advise you on the best option for your specific situation. Call us for a free site inspection and we'll talk through the pros and cons with no sales pressure. Whether you choose polished or epoxy, we'll make sure the job is done right the first time.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Concrete Grinding & Preparation for Melbourne Floors
blogPosts.excerpt: Concrete grinding is the foundation of any great floor finish. Learn why it matters, how it's done, and what to expect from the process.
body: Concrete grinding might not be the most glamorous part of a flooring project, but it's absolutely critical. Without proper grinding, your polished concrete or epoxy coating won't bond correctly, and the finish will look uneven or fail prematurely. At Nazcrete, we spend a lot of time on preparation because that's what separates a great floor from a mediocre one. Here's what you need to know about the grinding process in Melbourne.

Grinding uses diamond-impregnated discs to remove a thin layer of concrete. This smooths out imperfections, removes old coatings or glue, and opens up the pores of the concrete so sealers or epoxies can bond properly. The number of passes depends on the condition of the slab and the final finish you want. A coarse grind might be enough for a garage floor, while a living area destined for high-gloss polish needs multiple passes with finer grits.

Dust control is a huge deal, especially in occupied homes or businesses. At Nazcrete, we use industrial vacuums attached directly to our Husqvarna grinders. This captures over 95% of the dust at the source. We also seal off doorways with plastic sheeting and use air scrubbers if needed. This means you can stay in your South Melbourne home while we work, with no fine dust coating your furniture.

The grinding process also reveals any hidden issues with the slab — cracks, hollow spots, or weak concrete. We patch these as we go using high-strength repair mortars designed for concrete floors. This is one reason why a site inspection is so important. We can identify problem areas beforehand and include the repair work in your quote. No nasty surprises halfway through the job.

After grinding, we apply a densifier or hardener. This chemical seeps into the concrete and reacts with the free lime to form a harder, more durable surface. It also reduces dusting and makes the floor easier to clean. For polished concrete, the densifier is applied between grinding passes. For epoxy, it ensures the coating sticks properly. Skipping this step is a shortcut we never take.

If you're planning a concrete floor project in Melbourne, don't underestimate the importance of proper grinding and preparation. It's the foundation everything else sits on. The Nazcrete team has the gear and experience to do it right, whether you're after a simple seal or a showroom-quality polish. Contact us for a free quote and we'll talk through the process step by step.

blogPosts.title: Floor Removal Services in South Melbourne: What to Expect from Start to Finish
blogPosts.excerpt: Removing old vinyl, carpet, or tile flooring before a concrete polish? Here's how Nazcrete handles floor removal across Melbourne.
body: If you're planning to install polished concrete or epoxy flooring, the first step is often removing whatever's currently on the slab. That could be old vinyl sheets, carpet and underlay, ceramic tiles, or even multiple layers of glued-down flooring. Floor removal is messy, time-consuming work, but at Nazcrete we handle it as part of our full service. Here's what you can expect when you hire us for floor removal in South Melbourne or anywhere in the city.

We start with a site inspection to assess what's there. Vinyl and carpet are usually straightforward to pull up, but tile removal requires a heavy-duty scraper or grinder to get the thinset mortar off the concrete. Some old floors have asbestos-containing adhesives — we can identify these and advise you on safe removal protocols. If asbestos is present, we'll recommend a licensed specialist for that part before we proceed.

Our team brings in industrial floor scrapers and ride-on machines for large areas. For smaller rooms, we use hand tools and grinders. The goal is to get the slab completely clean and free of any debris, glue, or paper backing. Any leftover adhesive will prevent the sealer or epoxy from bonding, so we're thorough. We also use dust shrouds on our grinders to keep the mess contained.

Once the old floor is gone, we vacuum the entire area and check the slab's condition. Often, removing an old floor reveals cracks, patches, or uneven spots that need attention. We include these repairs in our quote so there's no extra cost later. If the slab is in good shape, we move straight to grinding and polishing. If it needs patching, we do that with high-strength concrete repair materials.

Timing depends on the size of the area and the type of flooring being removed. A standard 40-square-metre living room with carpet can be cleared in half a day. Tile removal takes longer because of the mortar. We'll give you an accurate timeline during the quote stage. Most clients can use their space again within 24 to 48 hours after removal, depending on whether patching or grinding is needed next.

Floor removal is often the most disruptive part of a concrete flooring project, but with the right team it doesn't have to be stressful. At Nazcrete, we work efficiently to minimise downtime and keep your property clean. If you're in South Melbourne, St Kilda, Richmond, or anywhere in Melbourne and need old flooring removed before a concrete polish or epoxy job, give us a call. We'll handle the hard work so you can enjoy your new floor.
